summary: One statically confirmed object-authorization issue in the supplied complete synthetic handler and contract.

findings.title: Invoice lookup omits owner authorization
findings.severity_rationale: Authenticated users can retrieve other owners private invoices when their IDs are known. Scope is this invoice endpoint, not all application data.
findings.confidence_rationale: The supplied code and explicit contract establish caller control, authentication-only middleware, private ownership and absence of hidden database policy.

evidence.quote: requireSession verifies a session and sets req.user={id,tenantId,role}; it only authenticates. db is an ordinary Prisma client with no extensions or row security. Invoices are private to ownerId. Users can know invoice IDs belonging to others.

findings.sink: Private invoice lookup and JSON response.
findings.missing_control: The lookup does not scope ownerId to the verified req.user.id.
controls_checked: requireSession authenticates according to the supplied contract; it does not authorize invoices.
The db contract excludes Prisma extensions and row security.
The not-found branch checks existence, not ownership.
preconditions: Caller has a valid ordinary session.
Caller knows an invoice ID owned by another user, as permitted by the supplied contract.
findings.attack_scenario: A signed-in caller selects another owners invoice ID and receives that private record.
findings.impact: Cross-owner disclosure of invoice data through the reviewed route.
findings.remediation: Use a query that includes the requested id and verified ownerId, preserving the stated private-owner policy. Return the same not-found response when no authorized record matches.
findings.regression_test: Proposed: an owner receives their invoice; a different owner with a valid session receives no invoice; nonexistent IDs return 404. Use synthetic accounts and assert response fields and unchanged records.

coverage_gaps: Synthetic single-route scope; no production repository, deployment or complete framework integration was reviewed.
